sections.label: Iswaran pay and MP allowance
sections.summary: Iswaran draws reduced ministerial pay of $8,500 monthly but full MP allowance of $192,500 yearly, and suspension requires a Parliament Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister informed this House on 2 August, while Minister Iswaran is interdicted from his Ministerial duties, he will draw a reduced pay of $8,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, Minister Iswaran continues to draw his full MP allowance of $192,500 per year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To do that, it must be done through a Motion in Parliament to suspend the Member from the service of Parliament.

sections.label: PSP no-pay leave proposal
sections.summary: PSP prefers suspend first, pay later, wanting investigated MPs or Ministers on no-pay leave with full back pay if cleared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, we prefer the second option of suspend first, pay later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is PSP's stance that an MP or Minister who is under investigation for corruption and suspended from official duties should be put on no-pay leave until the investigation or criminal case is concluded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the MP or Minister subsequently resumes their official duties after being cleared by the investigation or criminal case, they should be entitled to full back pay for the period during which they were on leave of absence.

sections.label: No-pay leave for investigated officials
sections.summary: PSP maintains investigated MPs or Ministers suspended from duties should get no pay until conclusion, receiving back pay only if cleared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Out of the many cases investigated, a much smaller number would result in an arrest, as had happened with Minister Iswaran.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We do, however, maintain that an MP or Minister who is under investigation for corruption and suspended from official duties should be put on no-pay leave until the investigation or criminal case is concluded and will only receive back pay if they are subsequently cleared by the investigation or criminal case.

sections.label: KOM conditional warning and investigations
sections.summary: KOM received a conditional warning in December 2017, and CPIB investigations concluded over five years later in January 2023 with a stern warning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In December 2017, KOM was served a conditional warning in lieu of prosecution by CPIB, with investigations continuing into the KOM executives involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The CPIB investigations only concluded more than five years later in January 2023, with a stern warning to the KOM executives.

sections.label: Grounds for Iswaran's suspension
sections.summary: Iswaran being under corruption investigation, arrested, and on leave of absence together make a strong case for suspension from Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Given that Minister Iswaran is: one, under investigation for corruption; two, placed under arrest; and three, put on leave of absence by the Prime Minister, we believe that these three factors together make a strong case for his suspension from Parliament.

sections.label: PSP voting against the Motion
sections.summary: PSP says suspending leads to a more desirable financial outcome, so it will vote against the Leader's Motion as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This clearly shows that suspending leads to a more desirable outcome financially.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, if the House were to vote on the Motion as a whole, PSP will be voting against the Motion moved by the Leader.

sections.label: Standing Order section reference
sections.summary: The speaker believes the relevant provision is section 56(5).

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: If I recall correctly, I believe it is section 56(5).

sections.label: Standing Order 59(5) quoted
sections.summary: The speaker corrects the reference to section 59(5), which preserves Parliament's power to proceed against a Member.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Oh, sorry, section 59(5) – "Nothing in this Standing Order shall be taken to deprive Parliament of the power of proceeding against any Member according to any resolution of Parliament."

sections.label: MP under investigation and arrest
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates that the Member is being investigated for corruption, under arrest and not performing MP duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Basically, let me reiterate that being investigated for corruption, under arrest and not performing his MP duties.

sections.label: Back pay if found innocent
sections.summary: The speaker says a provision will back pay the Minister if found innocent, with no presumption of guilt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Yes, of course, I do, which is why we are also making the provision to back pay the Minister if he should be found innocent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: There is no presumption of guilt here; just how to better use taxpayers' money.
